title: Discovery-Driven Planning: Managing Projects with High Uncertainty
excerpt: Traditional planning assumes you know the destination. Discovery-driven planning assumes you don't — and that's exactly why it works for the hardest problems PMs face.

title: The Pre-Mortem: How to Kill Your Product Before It Launches
excerpt: Most teams run post-mortems — autopsies after something has already died. The pre-mortem flips this: you imagine the failure before it happens, and you use that imagination to prevent it.

title: The Invisible Backlog: Why Your Team's Most Important Work Is the Stuff You Never Talk About
excerpt: Every team has two backlogs: the one in Jira and the one nobody writes down. The invisible backlog — unresolved friction, compounding complexity, eroded trust — is what actually kills velocity.

title: The Feedback Loop Illusion: Why You're Not Listening Even When You Think You Are
excerpt: Modern PMs collect feedback like it's a sport. Hundreds of survey responses. Dozens of user interviews. A Slack channel full of power user requests. But the volume of listening has almost nothing to do with the quality of what you actually hear.

title: The Second-Order Effect: How Today's Features Become Tomorrow's Constraints
excerpt: Every feature you ship is a decision about the future. Not just the future you intended — but the futures you accidentally locked yourself into.
